title: Closed points with finite separable residue field in a nonempty open of affine space
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The statement produces, in any nonempty open W of A^d_k over a field k, a closed point w with k inside kappa(w) finite separable (statement lines 4642-4647). The proof shrinks W to the complement of a single hypersurface V(f), then argues by contradiction: if no such point existed, f would vanish at every point of (k^sep)^d, which is absurd because k^sep is an infinite field (proof lines 4649-4654). The claim is H2: the only non-formal ingredient is the standard fact that a polynomial over an infinite field cannot vanish on the whole of (k^sep)^d, applied to the separable closure rather than to k.
